nodes.label: NestJS Documentation License
nodes.author: Kamil Mysliwiec
nodes.rationale: The NestJS documentation license is reproduced because Danet's docs heavily copy content from it; attribution is a licensing obligation, not just courtesy.

nodes.label: CookieStore
nodes.rationale: CookieStore is the simplest session store but requires an encryptionKey of at least 32 characters; sameSite Lax gives basic CSRF protection in modern browsers and httpOnly is recommended to avoid XSS exfiltration.

nodes.label: @Session() parameter decorator
nodes.rationale: hono_sessions' Session is essentially a map, so Danet types the injected value as Map<unknown, unknown> rather than inventing its own session abstraction.

nodes.label: QueueEvent message envelope {type, data}
nodes.rationale: Deno.kv has no message discrimination or channels, so listenQueue must consume every incoming message. Danet therefore wraps payloads in a {type, data} envelope and dispatches on `type` through a listeners map; non-Danet producers must format messages the same way.

nodes.label: Unhandled message type / redelivery
nodes.rationale: Only one method may listen to a given message type; unknown types throw 'Unhandled message type'. When a consumer throws, Deno.Kv redelivers with growing delay a few times before giving up.

nodes.label: Topic matching via Hono smart router
nodes.rationale: Reusing Hono's smart router on the message topic means websocket handlers can be as specific as HTTP endpoints, including params, optional segments and regex constraints, with no new routing concept for users to learn.
nodes.norm_label: topic matching via hono smart router

nodes.label: Broker back-pressure signal (false return)
nodes.rationale: sendMessage returns Promise<boolean>; `false` means the channel's write buffer is full, surfacing broker back-pressure to the caller instead of silently buffering.

nodes.label: Bootstrap injectable scanning for consumers
nodes.rationale: Consumers are wired at bootstrap by scanning every registered injectable for decorated methods, so a handler class must be declared in a module's `injectables` array to ever be instantiated and discovered.

nodes.label: Queue-name-as-contract decoupling
nodes.rationale: Because the queue name is the only contract between producer and consumer, the two sides need not live in the same application or even the same language; a JSON-encoded payload on a named durable queue is the whole interface.

nodes.label: One handler per message type
nodes.rationale: Like KV Queue's @OnQueueMessage, each @OnRabbitMQMessage handles exactly one queue and a queue may only have one handler in a given app. The constraint is deliberate: it keeps handlers small and single-purpose (SRP) rather than growing into dispatch switchboards.

nodes.label: Offload compression to a reverse proxy
nodes.rationale: For high-traffic production sites, compression should be handled by a reverse proxy such as Nginx rather than the application server; in that case compression middleware should not be used at all, to avoid paying the CPU cost twice in the app process.
nodes.norm_label: offload compression to a reverse proxy

nodes.label: EventEmitter is in-process only
nodes.rationale: EventEmitter events never leave the running instance because it is built on the EventTarget API. Crossing service boundaries with the same decorator ergonomics requires @danet/rabbitmq, or KV Queue for a durable in-Deno queue.

nodes.label: Observer pattern for in-app decoupling
nodes.rationale: Events decouple parts of an application because a single event can have multiple listeners that do not depend on each other; the emitter never needs to know who is listening.

nodes.label: Consumers run detached from their instance
nodes.rationale: The decorated method is handed to Deno.Kv.listenQueue as a plain function, so it loses its `this` binding and reaching for this.someService throws. Consumers must be self-contained and import the function doing the work.
nodes.norm_label: consumers run detached from their instance

nodes.label: Queues as a scaling design pattern
nodes.rationale: Queues smooth out processing peaks, break up monolithic tasks that would block the V8 event loop (e.g. audio transcoding), and provide a reliable communication channel across services, letting worker consumers scale independently of user-facing request handling.
nodes.norm_label: queues as a scaling design pattern

nodes.label: Handlers must return an EventTarget
nodes.rationale: Danet subscribes to the returned EventTarget only after the handler returns, so any event dispatched synchronously inside the handler is lost; events must be dispatched from a timer, interval or awaited callback.

nodes.label: Scheduled methods are looked for on injectables only
nodes.rationale: Only classes registered in a module's `injectables` array are scanned for scheduling decorators; controllers are never scanned, so scheduled methods must live on an injectable.
nodes.norm_label: scheduled methods are looked for on injectables only

nodes.label: topic/data message envelope
nodes.rationale: Every message received by a Danet app must carry a `topic` and `data`; that shape is what enables the topic and topic-matcher DX, and clients must JSON.stringify it before sending.

nodes.label: @Injectable() decorator (FR)
nodes.rationale: Ajoute des metadonnees declarant que la classe peut etre geree par le conteneur IoC de Danet.

nodes.label: @Module() decorator (FR)
nodes.rationale: Fournit les metadonnees (injectables, controllers, imports) que Danet utilise pour organiser la structure de l'application.

nodes.label: DynamicModule
nodes.rationale: A module created at run-time with the same properties as a static module plus a required `module` property naming the module class. All other properties are optional.

nodes.label: beforeControllerMethodIsCalled()
nodes.rationale: How a request-scoped injectable reaches the original request context; it may be async.

nodes.label: SCOPE enum
nodes.rationale: The enum is spelled SCOPE, in capitals; there is no `Scope` export.

nodes.label: OnAppBootstrap
nodes.rationale: Called once after all dependencies have been injected; may return a Promise or be async to defer application initialization.

nodes.label: OnAppClose
nodes.rationale: Only triggered if you explicitly call app.close(), right before shutting down connections.

nodes.label: Graphe d'application
nodes.rationale: Structure de donnees interne construite depuis le module racine pour resoudre les relations et dependances entre modules et fournisseurs.

nodes.label: SCOPE.GLOBAL (singleton)
nodes.rationale: Default and recommended: sharing injectables across consumers and requests means an instance is cached and initialized only once at startup. Safe in Deno because it does not use a request/response multi-threaded stateless model.

nodes.label: SCOPE.REQUEST
nodes.rationale: Exists for edge cases where request-based lifetime is desired: per-request caching in GraphQL, request tracking, multi-tenancy. Costs performance since an instance is built per request, though a well-designed app should not lose more than ~5% latency.

nodes.label: SCOPE.TRANSIENT
nodes.rationale: Each consumer receives a new dedicated instance, but transient does NOT propagate: a singleton injecting a transient stays singleton unless explicitly marked TRANSIENT itself.

nodes.label: Lifecycle hooks
nodes.rationale: Give visibility into key lifecycle events on injectables and controllers. Each hook is an interface; interfaces vanish after TypeScript compilation so they are technically optional, but implementing them buys strong typing and editor tooling.

nodes.label: Per-call execution context for gRPC
nodes.rationale: Every RPC call runs in its own execution context, so SCOPE.REQUEST injectables are instantiated fresh per call, just like in HTTP requests.

nodes.label: Danet pillars: Secure, Intuitive, Extensible
nodes.rationale: Secure: uses the latest Deno and TypeScript features for confidence and security. Intuitive: kept simple so developers focus on what matters. Extensible: other libraries and tools integrate without complications.

nodes.label: Section Vue d'ensemble (FR)
nodes.rationale: index.yml pilote la position (order: 99) et l'etat deplie (expanded: true) du groupe de sidebar; les sections principales sont ouvertes par defaut.

nodes.label: Danet home page
nodes.rationale: VitePress layout: home hero positioning Danet as 'the most mature backend framework for Deno' with the tagline 'Inspired by the best, inspiring you to be' - an explicit nod to its NestJS lineage.

nodes.label: Injection de dependance
nodes.rationale: Les dependances sont resolues par type grace a TypeScript; la fonction de connexion des instances est deleguee au runtime Danet plutot qu'ecrite imperativement. Les controleurs delegent aux injectables pour rester fins.

nodes.label: Enregistrement du fournisseur
nodes.rationale: Le service doit etre ajoute au tableau injectables du decorateur @Module() pour que Danet puisse resoudre les dependances du consommateur.

nodes.label: Module de fonctionnalites
nodes.rationale: Regrouper le code d'une fonctionnalite etablit des limites claires et aide a gerer la complexite quand l'application ou l'equipe grandit (principes SOLID).

nodes.label: Modules partages
nodes.rationale: Les modules sont des singletons par defaut: tout module qui importe un autre module partage la meme instance de ses fournisseurs, sans configuration.

nodes.label: DI fundamentals
nodes.rationale: DI is an inversion-of-control technique: instantiation is delegated to the IoC container instead of written imperatively. Dependency analysis happens at bootstrap and is transitive, resolving the graph bottom-up so developers never manage complex dependency graphs by hand.

nodes.label: Static module binding
nodes.rationale: All wiring information is declared up-front in host and consuming modules, which leaves the consumer no opportunity to influence how the host module's injectables are configured - the limitation dynamic modules exist to remove.

nodes.label: Scope hierarchy (REQUEST bubbling)
nodes.rationale: REQUEST scope bubbles up the injection chain: TodoController <- TodoService <- TodoRepository, if TodoService is request-scoped the controller becomes request-scoped while the repository below stays singleton. Controllers therefore never declare a scope - @Controller() takes only a path string.

nodes.label: Request-scoped classes excluded from lifecycle hooks
nodes.rationale: Request-scoped classes are not tied to the application lifecycle and their lifespan is unpredictable - created per request and deleted after the response - so lifecycle hooks are not triggered for them.
nodes.norm_label: request-scoped classes excluded from lifecycle hooks

nodes.label: @UseGuard() decorator
nodes.rationale: Accepte un ou plusieurs guards en une seule declaration, applicable au niveau controleur ou methode, pour attacher l'ensemble approprie sans repetition.

nodes.label: CookieStore
nodes.rationale: Le moyen le plus simple de gerer les sessions; requiert une encryptionKey d'au moins 32 caracteres. Les cookieOptions recommandees (sameSite Lax, httpOnly) protegent contre CSRF et XSS.

nodes.label: @Session() decorator
nodes.rationale: La Session de hono_session est essentiellement une carte, d'ou l'utilisation du type Map<unknown, unknown> dans la signature.

nodes.label: ExecutionContext
nodes.rationale: Provides details about the current execution process wherever Danet hands it out (guard canActivate(), middleware action()), including optional websocket and websocketTopic fields for the WebSocket message lifecycle.

nodes.label: getClass()
nodes.rationale: Returns the controller class TYPE, not an instance.

nodes.label: MetadataHelper.getMetadata()
nodes.rationale: Takes a metadata key and a context (decorator target): pass context.getHandler() for handler-level metadata, context.getClass() for controller-level metadata applying to all routes.

nodes.label: @SetMetadata() decorator
nodes.rationale: Attaches custom key/value metadata to route handlers, but using it directly in routes is discouraged: wrap it in a purpose-named custom decorator for readability and strong typing.

nodes.label: Garde (Guard)
nodes.rationale: Les gardes ont une seule responsabilite: decider si une requete atteint le gestionnaire de route, en fonction de conditions d'execution (permissions, roles, ACL). Separer l'autorisation du gestionnaire garde la logique metier propre.

nodes.label: Middleware Danet (FR)
nodes.rationale: Fonctions appelees avant le gestionnaire de route, avec acces a l'objet de contexte hono; elles peuvent executer du code arbitraire et modifier le contexte.

nodes.label: Sessions HTTP
nodes.rationale: Permettent de stocker des informations sur l'utilisateur a travers plusieurs requetes.

nodes.label: Compression des reponses
nodes.rationale: La compression reduit la taille du corps de reponse et accelere l'application, mais en production a fort trafic il est recommande de la decharger vers un proxy inverse (Nginx) plutot que d'utiliser un middleware applicatif.

nodes.label: Reflection and metadata pattern
nodes.rationale: Access to both the current class and handler reference is what lets guards and interceptors read decorator metadata and make authorization decisions generically.

nodes.label: Global guard on gRPC calls caveat
nodes.rationale: A guard registered under GLOBAL_GUARD runs for every transport. Reading context.req on a gRPC call throws and the client sees 'UNKNOWN: Cannot read properties of undefined'; branch on context.grpcMetadata instead. SetMetadata-based whitelists like @Public() keep working because getHandler() and getClass() are both set for gRPC calls.
nodes.norm_label: global guard on grpc calls caveat

nodes.rationale: Ships as a separate module (Danet-Swagger) rather than in core, and is explicitly flagged Alpha with many features missing - users are asked to file feature requests instead of expecting completeness.

nodes.label: Danet Philosophy
nodes.rationale: Provide an out-of-the-box application architecture allowing highly testable, scalable, loosely coupled and easily maintainable applications - the same goal as Nest, itself originally inspired by Angular.

nodes.label: Migration from Danet V1 to V2
nodes.rationale: V2 switched the internal HTTP engine from Oak to Hono for improved performance (backed by a published benchmark). The trade-off was deliberately kept to a single breaking change: the HTTPContext request/response shape.
nodes.community_name: Introduction and V1 to V2 Migration
nodes.norm_label: migration from danet v1 to v2

nodes.label: Native Hono middleware interop
nodes.rationale: Hono middleware is registered with application.use(), and must be registered BEFORE calling init(); otherwise it degrades into an 'execute if no route was matched' handler.
nodes.community_name: Introduction and V1 to V2 Migration

nodes.label: Section index.yml Config
nodes.rationale: Each section directory carries an index.yml with order/expanded/label controlling the sidebar group rather than an individual page.

nodes.label: Danet Framework
nodes.rationale: Fully TypeScript framework for building efficient, optimized, scalable back-end applications; abstracts plumbing so developers focus on business logic and architecture.

nodes.label: Hono (HTTP engine)
nodes.rationale: Danet runs on hono under the hood; other engines may be supported later, so the engine is treated as a swappable implementation detail.

nodes.label: NestJS
nodes.rationale: Explicit model for Danet: docs and even sentences are borrowed from Nest. Nest's architecture (itself originally inspired by Angular) is what Danet reproduces to bring out-of-the-box testable, scalable, loosely coupled, maintainable structure to Deno.

nodes.label: HTTPContext (v1 to v2)
nodes.rationale: The single breaking change of v2: HTTPContext stopped being a superset of the Oak context and became a superset of the Hono context, so context.response/context.request become context.res/context.req. context.res is the response object returned to the client unless the controller method returns something, in which case the return value wins.

nodes.label: @BodyType() / @QueryType()
nodes.rationale: The Swagger module scans @Body() and @Query() decorators and builds model definitions by reflection; these decorators override that inference when the definition must be explicit.

nodes.label: Parameter Decorators (@Req, @Res, @Param, @Header, @Body, @Query)
nodes.rationale: Dedicated decorators exist so handlers rarely need to reach into the raw request object. Each maps to a Hono context accessor (@Req -> ctx.req, @Res -> ctx.res, @Param -> context.params[key], @Body -> ctx.req.json()). @Query supports a value option of 'first' | 'last' | 'array'.

nodes.label: Danet Documentation Site
nodes.rationale: Docs-only repo, deliberately kept separate from the Danet framework source; VitePress site published to docs.danet.land so contributions are plain Markdown edits.

nodes.label: Danet Home Page (FR)
nodes.rationale: VitePress layout: home hero. Positions Danet as the most mature backend framework for Deno around three pillars: safe (latest Deno/TypeScript features), intuitive, extensible.

nodes.label: Fence-with-filename Code Blocks
nodes.rationale: Language plus filename on the fence info string renders as a tab label; the legacy @@filename() directive is deprecated. Examples import from jsr:@danet/core to match how users actually consume the published package.

nodes.label: ignoreDeadLinks
nodes.rationale: Dead-link checking is disabled so a broken link never fails the build; the trade-off is that links must be verified manually by the author.

nodes.label: Locale Mirrored Subtree
nodes.rationale: English is the root locale under src/*; translations live in a mirrored subtree (src/fr) excluded from the English sidebar via excludeDir. Restructuring an English page silently drifts the French tree out of sync, so drift must be reported rather than left implicit. pt.config.ts exists but is not mounted.

nodes.label: Page Frontmatter Convention
nodes.rationale: label drives the sidebar text and order is the in-section sort key. Ordering is DESCENDING: a higher order value appears higher in the sidebar, so new pages must pick an order relative to their siblings.

nodes.label: Auto-generated Sidebar
nodes.rationale: The sidebar is generated from the src/ directory tree via a vendored fork of vitepress-sidebar, so contributors never hand-edit navigation; adding a file with correct frontmatter is enough.

nodes.label: Switch to Hono in v2
nodes.rationale: v2 moved the internal HTTP engine to Hono for improved performance, evidenced by a published benchmark. The migration page's own prose is inconsistent, claiming v1 already used hono while describing the v1 context as an Oak superset.

nodes.label: Response Object Handling
nodes.rationale: Three escalating options. (1) Return a standard Response and Danet sends it as-is with no serialization, which is the direct route for Blob/ArrayBuffer/Uint8Array/ReadableStream bodies, but @HttpCode() is then ignored because the author owns the status. (2) Inject @Res() and mutate headers while still returning an object that Danet serializes and merges the headers into. (3) Inject the raw Hono context with @Context() for advanced helpers like c.header() and c.body(). Default behaviour serializes objects to JSON, sends strings as text/plain and uses status 200.

nodes.label: DynamicModule
nodes.rationale: Lets modules register and configure providers dynamically. Properties returned by forRoot() extend rather than override the static @Module() metadata, so statically declared and dynamically generated providers are both exported.

nodes.label: RabbitMQ.publish()
nodes.rationale: Asserts the exchange (creating it if missing) before publishing, and JSON-encodes the payload as persistent by default so messages survive broker restarts without extra configuration.

nodes.label: RabbitMQModule.forRoot()
nodes.rationale: Imported into the root module with at least an AMQP url plus optional prefetch; it connects to the broker and starts consuming during app.init(), so no extra boot step is needed.

nodes.label: RabbitMQ.sendMessage()
nodes.rationale: JSON-encodes the payload and creates the queue as durable if it does not exist yet, so publishing works without provisioning the queue up front.

nodes.label: RabbitMQ exchanges
nodes.rationale: A listener consumes a durable queue directly by default, which suffices for point-to-point messaging; exchanges are the opt-in that unlocks fan-out and topic routing. Binding options assert the queue, assert the exchange, and bind them with a routing key.

nodes.label: @danet/rabbitmq package
nodes.rationale: Brings the same DI-driven, decorator-based listener model as the built-in KV Queue and Events modules to a real broker, so switching transports does not mean learning a new programming model. Requires @danet/core >= 2.11.0.

nodes.label: RabbitMQ module limitations
nodes.rationale: One handler per queue within an app; no DTO validation because payloads are JSON.parsed as-is and the class-validator based @Body validation does not apply; no wildcard channel matching in the decorator because routing is delegated to RabbitMQ topic exchanges and routing-key patterns.

nodes.label: Cross-language wire format
nodes.rationale: KV Queue must wrap payloads as { type, data } because Deno.kv exposes a single global queue needing in-band routing. RabbitMQ has native queues and exchanges, so no wrapper is needed and the body is simply the JSON of the payload - which is what makes any producer in any language interoperable with a Danet handler.

nodes.label: frameMax connection workaround
nodes.rationale: amqplib still negotiates a 4096 byte frame by default while RabbitMQ 4.x refuses anything below 8192, so a 4.x broker fails with a bare 'read ECONNRESET' and no explanation. Fix is to request a bigger frame in the connection string (?frameMax=8192). Brokers on the 3.x line are unaffected.

nodes.label: Choosing between Events, KV Queue and RabbitMQ
nodes.rationale: Events is in-process pub/sub that lives and dies with a single instance, good for decoupling code inside one app. KV Queue is a durable queue backed by Deno.kv needing no extra infrastructure but tied to Deno and a single global queue. RabbitMQ is a battle-tested broker shared across services and languages with native queues, exchanges, routing and acknowledgements - reach for it when messages must cross service or language boundaries.
nodes.norm_label: choosing between events, kv queue and rabbitmq

nodes.label: HTTPContext
nodes.rationale: HTTPContext moved from being a superset of Oak's context to a superset of Hono's context, so context.response/context.request became context.res/context.req. A controller method's returned value takes precedence over context.res.

nodes.label: @ApiProperty() decorator
nodes.rationale: Class properties are invisible to the SwaggerModule unless annotated; enums must be declared manually via the enum option because the value set cannot be reflected.

nodes.label: @ReturnedType() decorator
nodes.rationale: Return types are inferred from the method signature, but arrays cannot be reflected, so @ReturnedType(Todo, true) exists to declare array returns explicitly.

nodes.label: SwaggerModule reflection of parameters
nodes.rationale: Scans route handlers for @Body() and @Query() decorators and uses reflection to build model definitions automatically, so the spec follows the code.

nodes.label: Parameter decorators (@Req, @Res, @Context, @Param, @Header, @Body, @Query)
nodes.rationale: Dedicated decorators exist so handlers rarely need to grab properties off the raw request object; each maps to a specific slice of the Hono context (ctx.req, ctx.res, context.params, ctx.req.json(), ...).

nodes.label: Zod schema support in OpenAPI module
nodes.norm_label: zod schema support in openapi module

nodes.label: DTO (Data Transfer Object)
nodes.rationale: A DTO defines how data is sent over the network, expressed as a plain class carrying type validation decorators so the schema doubles as runtime validation.

nodes.label: Response object handling
nodes.rationale: Three escalating options: return a value and let Danet serialize it (objects to JSON, strings to text/plain, status 200); return a standard Response for full control, in which case @HttpCode() is ignored because you set the status yourself; or inject @Res()/@Context() to only tweak headers while keeping automatic serialization.

nodes.label: @Inject() decorator
nodes.rationale: Constructor-based injection requires a class-name dependency; @Inject() takes the token so string- or symbol-valued providers can be injected too.

nodes.label: useValue provider
nodes.rationale: Useful for injecting a constant value, putting an external library into the container, or replacing a real implementation with a mock. Works with any structurally compatible object thanks to TypeScript structural typing.

nodes.label: 'CONFIG_OPTIONS' token
nodes.rationale: Binds the run-time options object to the IoC container so it can be injected into ConfigService. Best practice is to define it as an exported constant or Symbol in a separate file.

nodes.label: ConfigModule
nodes.rationale: A generic 'plugin'-like module: externalizing configuration keeps application source code independent of configuration parameters across deployments (dev/staging DBs), but a generic module must be customizable by its consumer, which is why it is made dynamic.

nodes.label: static register() method
nodes.rationale: Can have any name but convention is forRoot() or register(); it accepts arbitrary options and must return a DynamicModule so its result can sit in an imports array.

nodes.label: Non-class-based provider tokens
nodes.rationale: Strings, JavaScript symbols or TypeScript enums can serve as DI tokens for flexibility. Best practice is to define tokens in a separate constants.ts file rather than inlining string literals.

nodes.label: Injectable declaration order rule
nodes.rationale: A useValue injectable must be declared BEFORE the injectables that depend on it. Danet resolves the injectables array in order; a consumer reached first makes the container try to instantiate the value as a class, failing with `TypeError: actualType is not a constructor`. useClass injectables are unaffected.

nodes.label: @Body(schema) from @danet/zod
nodes.rationale: Passing the schema to the decorator validates the request body automatically and doubles as the source of truth for OpenAPI generation, so a schema is declared once and serves both purposes.

nodes.label: extendZodWithOpenApi
nodes.rationale: Zod must be extended with @anatine/zod-openapi before OpenAPI definitions can be generated, and each schema needs an .openapi({title}) so the model can be named in the definition.

nodes.label: @ReturnedSchema decorator
nodes.rationale: Declares the endpoint's response schema; a second `true` argument marks the response as an array, since the return type alone is erased at runtime.

nodes.label: SwaggerModule
nodes.rationale: The SwaggerModule is in Alpha with many features missing; it generates the API document by searching route handlers for @Body() and @Query() decorators from @danet/zod and creating the corresponding model definitions.

nodes.label: Zod schema + z.infer typing pattern
nodes.rationale: Declaring `type X = z.infer<typeof X>` alongside the schema gives runtime validation and the static DTO type from a single declaration, avoiding class-based DTO duplication.

nodes.label: zod / @anatine/zod-openapi pinned versions
nodes.rationale: The Swagger module pins zod@3.23.8 and @anatine/zod-openapi@2.2.6; user projects must match those versions for schema extension to interoperate.

nodes.label: @Render() decorator
nodes.rationale: La valeur de retour de la methode de route est passee au modele: les proprietes de l'objet correspondent aux espaces reserves du template.

nodes.label: SwaggerModule.createDocument()
nodes.rationale: Returns a serializable OpenAPI Document object, so it can be hosted over HTTP or saved as JSON/YAML and consumed elsewhere.

nodes.label: SpecBuilder
nodes.rationale: Structures a base OpenAPI document (title, description, version, security definitions) that createDocument then completes with all discovered HTTP routes.

nodes.label: @ApiSecurity() decorator
nodes.rationale: Generic escape hatch for declaring an operation's security mechanism; the popular schemes (basic, bearer) are built in so most users never need to define them manually.

nodes.label: SpecBuilder security definitions
nodes.rationale: Every security decorator must be paired with a matching addSecurity/addBasicAuth/addBearerAuth/addOAuth2/addCookieAuth call on the base document before the app runs, otherwise the scheme is undeclared.

nodes.label: @Controller() decorator
nodes.rationale: The optional path prefix lets related routes be grouped and stops the shared path segment from being repeated on every handler.

nodes.label: DanetApplication
nodes.rationale: Docs advise wrapping construction in a bootstrap() function returning the application instance, because that makes testing easier: the test can grab the instance and listen on a random port.

nodes.label: GLOBAL_GUARD token
nodes.rationale: Registering a guard in the module's injectables under the GLOBAL_GUARD token applies it to every controller and route handler in the application.

nodes.label: @Module() decorator
nodes.rationale: Takes a single metadata object with injectables, controllers and imports, which Danet uses to organize the application structure.

nodes.label: @Render() decorator
nodes.rationale: Names the template; the handler's returned object becomes the template's variable bag, so object keys must match the placeholders.

nodes.label: app.useStaticAssets()
nodes.rationale: Registers a folder on the DanetApplication instance so its files (images, assets) are served directly; called after init with an absolute path.

nodes.label: Routing mechanism
nodes.rationale: Decorators attach metadata to classes so Danet can build a routing map; the handler method name is arbitrary and carries no meaning, the route path is the concatenation of controller prefix and method path.

nodes.label: Exceptions layer
nodes.rationale: A built-in global exception filter catches every unhandled exception so users always get a friendly response; exceptions carrying statusCode and message are passed through, anything unrecognized becomes a generic 500 Internal server error.

nodes.label: Injectable scopes
nodes.rationale: Default lifetime is synchronized with the application lifecycle: every dependency is instantiated at bootstrap and destroyed at shutdown, with request-scoped lifetime available as an opt-in.

nodes.label: Provider registration
nodes.rationale: A provider must be listed in a module's injectables array before Danet can resolve consumers that depend on it.

nodes.label: Application graph
nodes.rationale: The internal data structure built from the root module, used to resolve module and provider relationships and dependencies.

nodes.label: Feature module
nodes.rationale: Groups code for one application domain to keep boundaries clear and manage complexity as the application and team grow - an application of SOLID at module granularity.

nodes.label: Shared modules (singletons)
nodes.rationale: Modules are singletons by default, so every module is automatically a shared module and importers all receive the same provider instance with no extra work.

nodes.label: Handlebars templating engine
nodes.rationale: Integrated so Danet can serve simple MVC apps rendering HTML, not only JSON APIs.

nodes.label: views directory convention
nodes.rationale: Convention is /views, /views/layouts and /views/partials at project root with a main.hbs default layout; setViewEngineDir() exists as the escape hatch for a different location.

nodes.label: prefetch (QoS)
nodes.rationale: Caps how many unacknowledged messages the broker delivers at once, which is the mechanism for spreading work across multiple consumer instances.

nodes.label: Controller scopes
nodes.rationale: Almost everything is shared across incoming requests (connection pools, singleton services with global state); request-scoped lifetime is an edge case reserved for request tracking or multi-tenancy.

nodes.label: Modules do not encapsulate injectables
nodes.rationale: Any injectable can be injected from any module as long as it has been resolved - injectables are registered globally, like Angular. The docs state explicitly that this will change in the future, and the `exports` metadata key is commented out pending that change.

nodes.label: Automatic acknowledgements
nodes.rationale: A resolving handler acks; a throwing handler nacks WITHOUT requeue. Requeue is deliberately avoided so a failing message goes to a dead-letter policy instead of being redelivered in a hot loop.

nodes.label: noAck consume option
nodes.rationale: noAck: true is AMQP auto-acknowledge: the broker forgets the message the moment it leaves the queue. Danet detects the flag and skips its own ack/nack, and the user must not ack either - doing so closes the channel with 406 PRECONDITION_FAILED - unknown delivery tag. Trade-off: messages are lost if the handler throws or the process dies mid-work, so the docs say leave noAck alone unless losing messages is acceptable.

nodes.label: useClass provider
nodes.rationale: Lets a token resolve to a class chosen dynamically, e.g. DevelopmentConfigService vs ProductionConfigService based on the ENVIRONMENT variable, overriding any default implementation declared elsewhere.

nodes.label: Standard injectables shorthand
nodes.rationale: injectables: [TodoService] is shorthand for { token: TodoService, useClass: TodoService } - a convenience for the common case where the token requests an instance of the class of the same name. Caveat: class tokens work at runtime but `token` is typed as string, so writing the long form explicitly makes TypeScript complain; prefer a string constant until the type is widened.

nodes.label: SSEMessage interface
nodes.rationale: The interface mirrors the SSE specification fields (data, id, event, retry). `data` may be an object because Danet JSON.stringify's it before writing, since the SSE wire format only carries text.

nodes.label: close event terminates the stream
nodes.rationale: Danet holds the connection open until an event whose `event` field is `close` arrives; without one the connection stays open indefinitely, so producers own stream termination.

nodes.label: Absence d'encapsulation des injectables
nodes.rationale: Le module n'encapsule pas ses injectables: on peut injecter depuis n'importe quel module des lors qu'il a ete resolu. C'est pourquoi il n'y a pas de cle exports. Le document annonce que cela changera dans le futur.

nodes.label: No exports key on @Module()
nodes.rationale: Danet modules do not encapsulate their injectables today, so there is no exports key; once an injectable has been resolved it is available to any consumer.

nodes.label: @WebSocket() parameter decorator
nodes.rationale: Needed to push a message outside the normal request/response flow, for example broadcasting to other clients.

nodes.label: WebSocketInstance (WebSocket & {id})
nodes.rationale: The id is stable for the lifetime of the connection, which is what makes a map of connected clients possible.

nodes.label: ExecutionContext
nodes.rationale: Supplied wherever the current execution process matters (guard canActivate(), middleware action()). getHandler() returns a reference to the handler about to run and getClass() returns the controller TYPE (not the instance); access to both is what makes decorator metadata reachable from guards and interceptors.

nodes.label: MetadataHelper
nodes.rationale: Static getMetadata(key, target) reads decorator metadata. Passing context.getHandler() reads method-level metadata, passing context.getClass() reads controller-level metadata.

nodes.label: @Roles() Custom Decorator
nodes.rationale: Canonical example of wrapping @SetMetadata('roles', ...) in a typed decorator; can be applied at controller level to cover every route of the class.

nodes.label: @SetMetadata()
nodes.rationale: Attaches custom key/value metadata to route handlers, but using it directly in routes is discouraged; wrapping it in a purpose-built decorator is cleaner, more readable and strongly typed.

nodes.label: beforeControllerMethodIsCalled
nodes.rationale: Hook giving a request-scoped provider access to the originating HttpContext; may be async.

nodes.label: Injection Scope
nodes.rationale: Almost everything is shared across incoming requests because Deno does NOT follow the multi-threaded stateless request/response model, so singletons are safe by construction. Scopes exist only for the special cases (per-request caching, request tracking, multi-tenancy).

nodes.label: Scope.GLOBAL
nodes.rationale: Default and recommended: one shared instance whose lifetime tracks the application, so initialization runs once at bootstrap and the instance can be cached.

nodes.label: Scope.REQUEST
nodes.rationale: A fresh instance per incoming request, released afterwards. Costs performance because an instance must be constructed per request, so it is discouraged unless required; a well-designed app should stay within roughly 5% extra latency.

nodes.label: Lifecycle Hooks
nodes.rationale: Registered on injectables and controllers to observe and act on key application events. Hook interfaces are technically optional (they vanish after TypeScript compilation) but implementing them buys strong typing and editor tooling.

nodes.label: OnAppBootstrap
nodes.rationale: Called once after every dependency has been injected. Returning a Promise (or marking it async) defers the whole application initialization until it settles.

nodes.label: OnAppClose
nodes.rationale: Fires only on an explicit app.close(), just before connections are closed.

nodes.label: OpenAPI Specification
nodes.rationale: Language-agnostic definition format for RESTful APIs; Danet generates it from decorators rather than requiring a hand-written spec.

nodes.label: SpecBuilder
nodes.rationale: Fluent builder for the base OpenAPI document (title, description, version) and for security definitions that decorators reference by name.

nodes.label: SwaggerModule
nodes.rationale: Dedicated @danet/swagger module, explicitly flagged ALPHA with many features missing across every OpenAPI page. createDocument(application, spec) reflects all endpoints automatically; setup(path, application, document) mounts the Swagger UI. The document is a serializable OpenAPI Document, so it can be saved as JSON/YAML instead of served over HTTP, and is downloadable at /api/json.

nodes.label: @Tag()
nodes.rationale: Attaches a controller or an individual endpoint to an OpenAPI tag; in OpenAPI terms paths are endpoints and operations are the HTTP methods acting on them.

nodes.label: @ApiSecurity()
nodes.rationale: Generic escape hatch naming a security mechanism that must first be declared on the base document via SpecBuilder.addSecurity(). The common schemes are built in, so manual declaration is only needed for unusual ones.

nodes.label: @ApiProperty()
nodes.rationale: Class properties are invisible to the Swagger module unless annotated. Enums cannot be detected by reflection, so the enum values must be listed manually via @ApiProperty({ enum: [...] }). @Optional() marks optional properties.

nodes.label: @Controller()
nodes.rationale: Mandatory decorator defining a controller. Decorators bind classes to metadata, letting Danet build a routing map. The optional path prefix groups related routes and removes duplication; the final route path concatenates the controller prefix with the method decorator path. Handler method names are arbitrary and carry no meaning for Danet.

nodes.label: CreateTodoDto
nodes.rationale: A DTO is a class with type-validation decorators defining how data is sent; a body that violates it produces a 400 NotValidBodyException listing per-property reasons.

nodes.label: HTTP Method Decorators
nodes.rationale: @Get, @Post, @Put, @Delete, @Patch cover the standard verbs and @All handles every verb at once. A handler returning a plain value yields status 200.

nodes.label: Controller Scopes (FR overview)
nodes.rationale: Notes that nearly everything is shared across requests and that request-scoped controller lifetimes exist for request tracking and multi-tenancy; the page defers the full explanation to a future dedicated page.

nodes.label: Validatte
nodes.rationale: Savory's own validation library (jsr:@danet/validatte) used to validate the DTO schema against the received body, one decorator per attribute.

nodes.label: @Catch()
nodes.rationale: Binds metadata telling Danet which single exception type this filter handles. Omitting @Catch() entirely is the documented way to catch every unhandled exception regardless of type.

nodes.label: ExceptionFilter
nodes.rationale: Exists to give full control over the exceptions layer when the built-in filter is not enough, e.g. to add logging or vary the JSON shape on dynamic factors.

nodes.label: Built-in Global Exception Filter
nodes.rationale: Danet ships an exceptions layer that catches every unhandled exception and returns a user-comprehensible response. Unrecognized exceptions (lacking statusCode and message) collapse to a default 500 JSON body; any thrown exception carrying statusCode and message is surfaced faithfully instead.

nodes.label: HttpException Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: A standard set of exceptions inheriting HttpException covering the common HTTP errors (BadRequestException, UnauthorizedException, NotFoundException, ForbiddenException, ImATeapotException, ...).

nodes.label: @UseFilter()
nodes.rationale: Takes the filter CLASS rather than an instance, leaving instantiation to the framework so dependency injection works. Can be applied at method, controller or global level.

nodes.label: Scope Hierarchy Bubbling
nodes.rationale: REQUEST scope propagates UP the injection chain: a controller depending on a request-scoped provider becomes request-scoped itself. Dependencies of that provider are unaffected and stay singleton (TodoController <- TodoService <- TodoRepository).

nodes.label: Request-scoped Hook Exclusion
nodes.rationale: Lifecycle hooks never fire for request-scoped classes: those classes are not tied to the application lifecycle and their lifetime is unpredictable, being created per request and discarded once the response is sent.

nodes.label: HMAC shared secret vs RSA/ECDSA key pair
nodes.rationale: The private/public key option (RSA, ECDSA) is the preferred method because a leaked shared secret on the client forces a server-side secret rotation, whereas a leaked public key does not compromise the private key. HMAC is shown only because it is conceptually easier to start with.

nodes.label: Null Authorization header guard clause
nodes.rationale: headers.get() returns null when the header is absent, which is the common unauthenticated case; checking before use keeps the guard from throwing and returning a 500 where the caller should have received a plain denial.

nodes.label: HTTP / WebSocket controller parity
nodes.rationale: Danet abstracts implementation details so the same components (DI, decorators, exception filters, pipes, guards, interceptors) run across HTTP and WebSockets; @Body and @Param behave identically, making the two controller kinds almost permutable for the user.

nodes.label: Danet CLI
nodes.rationale: Projects created with the CLI embody best-practice architectural patterns to encourage well-structured apps. Installed as a global Deno command, conventionally named `danet`.

nodes.label: danet develop / danet start
nodes.rationale: develop runs with file watching, start runs without.

nodes.label: Database Provider Options
nodes.rationale: danet new prompts interactively for mongodb / postgres / in-memory and generates the matching code; --mongodb, --postgres and --in-memory flags exist for non-interactive use.

nodes.label: deno.json Import Map
nodes.rationale: Generated files import from the bare `@danet/core` specifier, mapped in the deno.json created by danet new; hand-built projects must add that entry themselves.

nodes.label: --path option
nodes.rationale: Defaults to `src`. It also relocates where a generated module looks for its root module, so `--path src/features` registers into src/features/app.module.ts, not src/app.module.ts.

nodes.label: Schematics (module, controller, service)
nodes.rationale: Each component lives in its own folder following the Danet folder convention. The name is normalized to kebab-case for the folder and PascalCase for the class, so user-profile / userProfile / UserProfile all converge on the same output.

nodes.label: --skip-import
nodes.rationale: Opt-out escape hatch from automatic module wiring.

nodes.label: danet bundle
nodes.rationale: Produces a single JS file containing all project source. Any bundler works as long as it handles emitDecoratorMetadata, which decorator-driven Danet depends on. Argument is the output name, input is --entrypoint (default run.ts); output goes to ./bundle, deleted and recreated each run.

nodes.label: danet deploy
nodes.rationale: One-command path: creates the project if it does not exist. The FIRST deployment goes to production; every later one is a preview with its own URL, so promoting a later build requires bundling and calling deployctl --prod manually.

nodes.label: Deno Deploy
nodes.rationale: Distributed edge runtime deeply integrated with V8, chosen for minimal latency and no configuration; deploys in under a second.

nodes.label: Deno Deploy GitHub Action Workflow
nodes.rationale: Danet projects must choose the 'Github Action' CD mode rather than automatic push deployment, because a bundling build step has to run before deploying. id-token: write permission is needed for auth with Deno Deploy, which removes the need for a token secret.

nodes.label: CLI Danet (FR)
nodes.rationale: French translation of the CLI page; predates the generate/scaffolding section, still describing scaffolding as a future capability.

nodes.label: Deno Deploy (FR)
nodes.rationale: French page still documents hard-coded pricing tiers and Deno v1.x workflow pinning, which the English page deliberately removed in favour of linking the pricing source.

nodes.label: @ReturnedType()
nodes.rationale: MANDATORY because SWC, Deno's TypeScript compiler, does not emit design:return metadata, so the return type cannot be reflected. Pass true as the second argument when the route returns an array.

nodes.label: bootstrap() / DanetApplication
nodes.rationale: Exporting a bootstrap function that returns the initialized DanetApplication instead of listening immediately makes testing easier: tests can grab the instance and listen on a random port.

nodes.label: @Module()
nodes.rationale: Controllers always belong to a module; Danet will not instantiate a controller it has not seen in a module's controllers array. Module metadata is what Danet reflects on to know what to mount.

nodes.label: Database Configuration (env vars / dotenv)
nodes.rationale: Two interchangeable ways to supply DB_NAME/DB_HOST/DB_PORT/DB_USERNAME/DB_PASSWORD: real environment variables or a .env file. dotenv works because Deno supports it natively, and a .env.example ships with the project.

nodes.label: Danet Installation (Premiers pas)
nodes.rationale: The CLI is presented as the easiest way to set up a project; danet new scaffolds a CRUD TODO API backed by MongoDB, Postgres or in-memory. Requires Deno >= 1.24.3.

nodes.label: Automatic Module Wiring
nodes.rationale: Generated components are registered automatically so the user never hand-edits @Module: controllers go into `controllers`, services into `injectables`, modules into the root app.module.ts `imports`. Wiring is skipped silently (no error) when the target module file is missing, which means the module must be generated before its controller or service.

nodes.label: canActivate()
nodes.rationale: Retourne un booleen (sync ou via Promise): true traite la requete, false la refuse. Danet utilise cette valeur de retour comme unique point de controle.

nodes.label: @Middleware() decorator
nodes.rationale: Prend autant de middlewares que necessaire; l'ordre de gauche a droite determine l'ordre d'execution sequentielle.

nodes.label: @GrpcController()
nodes.rationale: Binds controller methods to the RPCs of a Protobuf service definition while reusing everything else Danet offers: DI, guards, middleware, exception filters.

nodes.label: @GrpcMetadata()
nodes.rationale: gRPC metadata is the equivalent of HTTP headers. Because a metadata key may repeat, @GrpcMetadata('key') yields an ARRAY, not a string; omitting the key returns the whole Metadata object.

nodes.label: @GrpcMethod()
nodes.rationale: The RPC name defaults to the method name; pass an explicit name to override. The returned value is serialized against the RPC's response message type.

nodes.label: loadProto()
nodes.rationale: Thin wrapper around @grpc/proto-loader. The path is resolved by the process, not the module, so a relative './greeter.proto' only works when the cwd happens to be right; anchoring on import.meta.url makes it independent of where the app is started.

nodes.label: HttpException (custom gRPC message)
nodes.rationale: The built-in exceptions take no constructor argument, so the client only reads a generic description; throwing HttpException directly lets you choose both the status and the details text the caller receives.

nodes.label: @danet/grpc package
nodes.rationale: Adds a native gRPC transport built on @grpc/grpc-js. It is a real native server (HTTP/2 + Protobuf) rather than gRPC-Web or a proxy, so any gRPC client in any language can talk to it. Controllers reuse the entire Danet pipeline and the gRPC server binds its own port alongside the HTTP server.

nodes.label: GrpcServer
nodes.rationale: Must be constructed BEFORE app.init() so the transport can claim its controllers during bootstrap; constructing it after init() hands gRPC controllers to the HTTP router, which has no path to register them under and aborts the boot with a TypeError.

nodes.label: Exception filters on gRPC
nodes.rationale: Filters run for gRPC calls just like HTTP; if a filter returns a value, that value is sent back as the RPC reply instead of an error.

nodes.label: Danet exception to gRPC status mapping
nodes.rationale: Built-in HTTP exceptions are mapped to the closest gRPC status (BadRequest->INVALID_ARGUMENT, Unauthorized->UNAUTHENTICATED, Forbidden->PERMISSION_DENIED, NotFound->NOT_FOUND, Conflict->ALREADY_EXISTS, PreconditionFailed->FAILED_PRECONDITION, TooManyRequests->RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, InternalServerError->INTERNAL, NotImplemented->UNIMPLEMENTED, ServiceUnavailable->UNAVAILABLE, GatewayTimeout->DEADLINE_EXCEEDED). Any other error maps to UNKNOWN.
nodes.norm_label: danet exception to grpc status mapping

nodes.label: Middleware fonctionnel
nodes.rationale: Quand un middleware n'a ni membres, ni methodes supplementaires, ni dependances, une simple fonction suffit; la classe n'apporte alors rien et l'alternative fonctionnelle est recommandee.

nodes.label: Transport-agnostic middleware constraint
nodes.rationale: Middleware that reads ctx.req / ctx.res has nothing to operate on during a gRPC call; the same caveat applies to WebSocket controllers.

nodes.label: gRPC transport limitations
nodes.rationale: Unary RPCs only for now - streaming RPCs are skipped and clients calling them receive UNIMPLEMENTED (support planned). Transport-agnostic middleware only. No DTO validation on the payload because the Protobuf schema IS the contract, so class-validator based validation used by @Body does not apply to @GrpcPayload.

nodes.label: gRPC requirements (Deno 2.8+, @danet/core 2.11.0+)
nodes.rationale: Deno 2.8+ is required because server-side gRPC relies on node:http2 trailer support; @danet/core 2.11.0 is the release that exposes the transport hook this package plugs into.

nodes.label: @Catch() decorator
nodes.rationale: Binds metadata declaring which exception type the filter targets; omitting the decorator entirely is the documented way to catch every unhandled exception regardless of type.

nodes.label: ExceptionFilter interface
nodes.rationale: Exists for cases where the built-in filter is not enough - custom logging or a different JSON schema based on dynamic factors - giving full control over the flow and the response body.

nodes.label: @UseFilter() decorator
nodes.rationale: Takes the filter class rather than an instance, leaving instantiation to the framework so dependency injection still applies. Can be applied method-scoped or controller-scoped.

nodes.label: app.useGlobalExceptionFilter()
nodes.rationale: Takes an already-built instance (e.g. new ErrorFilter(app.get(SimpleService))), so global filters can be wired with resolved dependencies after init.

nodes.label: AuthGuard interface
nodes.rationale: Guards have a single responsibility: decide at run-time whether a request reaches the route handler, based on permissions, roles or ACLs. That makes them the designated place for authorization.

nodes.label: canActivate()
nodes.rationale: Must return a boolean (sync or via Promise): true lets the request through, false makes Danet deny it. Async support exists because token validation often needs I/O.

nodes.label: @UseGuard() decorator
nodes.rationale: Accepts a comma-separated list so a whole set of guards is applied in one declaration; placed on a class it covers every handler, placed on a method it covers only that one.

nodes.label: @Injectable() decorator
nodes.rationale: Attaches metadata declaring the class can be managed by the Danet IoC container, so wiring up instances is delegated to the runtime instead of being done by hand.

nodes.label: TodoService
nodes.rationale: Controllers should handle HTTP and delegate complex work to injectables, which is why data storage and retrieval live in a service rather than the controller.

nodes.label: DanetMiddleware interface
nodes.rationale: Middleware runs before the route handler with access to Hono's context; it can execute arbitrary code and mutate the context object.

nodes.label: @Middleware() decorator
nodes.rationale: Applies at controller or method level and accepts several middleware; they execute sequentially in left-to-right argument order.

nodes.label: NestJS (inspiration)
nodes.rationale: Nest is treated as the 'hero' Danet looks up to: Danet borrows its architecture, documentation and wording deliberately, crediting Nest as more mature.

nodes.label: Dependency Injection
nodes.rationale: Thanks to TypeScript, dependencies are resolved purely by constructor parameter type; in the normal singleton case an existing instance is reused rather than recreated.

nodes.label: IoC container
nodes.rationale: Resolves relationships between injectables and supports plain values, classes, and synchronous or asynchronous factories - more powerful than plain type-based constructor injection.

nodes.label: Functional middleware
nodes.rationale: A class with no members, methods or dependencies gains nothing from being a class - the docs recommend the simpler plain-function form whenever the middleware needs no dependencies.

nodes.label: getSecondaryKeys()
nodes.rationale: Deno KV has no secondary indexes, so repositories declare their secondary keys once in getSecondaryKeys and the base class writes and updates every entry on create/updateOne; the user never has to manage index consistency by hand.

nodes.label: Repository<T> interface
nodes.rationale: A single generic repository interface (getAll/getById/create/updateOne/deleteOne/deleteAll) is shared by every provider so application code can swap MongoDB for Deno KV without rewriting call sites; provider-specific extras (getOne, filters, secondary keys) live on the concrete subclasses.

nodes.label: InMemoryThrottlerStorage
nodes.rationale: The default storage evicts expired windows so the store never grows unbounded, but it is process-local and therefore not shared across instances in a horizontally-scaled deployment.
nodes.community_name: Databases KV Queue and Throttler Storage

nodes.label: ThrottlerStorage interface
nodes.rationale: Storage is an interface so counters can be shared across horizontally scaled instances via Redis or Deno.KV; implementations own window expiry and must start a fresh window once the previous one has elapsed.

nodes.label: CronExpression enum
nodes.rationale: CronExpression is inherited from @nestjs/schedule, which uses six fields with a leading seconds field, while Deno.cron parses only five, numbers days of week 1-7 and months 1-12. Entries such as EVERY_WEEK, EVERY_WEEKEND, EVERY_YEAR, EVERY_30_MINUTES_BETWEEN_* and the MONDAY_TO_FRIDAY_* group are rejected with 'Invalid cron schedule' at boot.

nodes.label: ScheduleModule
nodes.rationale: Job registration happens on the onAppBootstrap lifecycle hook so that all modules have loaded and declared their scheduled jobs before anything is registered with Deno.

nodes.label: collectionName constructor attribute
nodes.rationale: Every repository sets collectionName in its constructor so one abstract base can serve any collection/table/KV prefix without per-entity code duplication.
nodes.community_name: Databases KV Queue and Throttler Storage

nodes.label: onAppBootstrap / onAppClose connection lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Each provider service implements the Danet lifecycle hooks so database connections open when the app boots and close when it shuts down, tying connection management to the framework lifecycle instead of module import side effects.

nodes.label: Per-route counter keying
nodes.rationale: The storage key is built from throttler name + caller + controller class + handler name, so budgets are per route rather than per application: exhausting GET /todo leaves GET /todo/:id untouched.
nodes.community_name: Databases KV Queue and Throttler Storage

nodes.label: Job names are method names and must be unique
nodes.rationale: The job name is the method name, and Deno.cron refuses duplicates, so two methods named cleanUp() in two different injectables fail at boot with 'Cron with this name already exists'.
